newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan shinkin banks to bail out troubled Musashino.
newsitem.headline: Japan shinkin banks to bail out troubled Musashino.

text.p: Zenshinren Bank, a central organisation of Japanese "shinkin" banks, said in a statement issued at midnight on Monday that it would bail out Tokyo-based Musashino Shinkin Bank, which is reeling under problem loans.

Musashino, a credit association which takes deposits and lends money to mainly members, said on Monday it faced financial problems with unrecoverable loans totalling 24.2 billion yen and had given up efforts to restructure on its own.
Zenshinren Bank said it and the Tokyo shinkin bank association had discussed measures to bail out Musashino, including a merger with a healthy shinkin bank.

Zenshinren Bank said shinkin banks would cope with the problem of Musashino even if reported merger talks with Johnan Shinkin Bank, the nation's biggest credit association, failed to reach an agreement.
Shinkin banks are small credit associations which take deposits and lend mainly to members. They are supervised by the Ministry of Finance.
A Johnan Shinkin official said on Monday it had received an offer to absorb the troubled Musashino from the Zenshinren Bank, but said the offer failed to meet Johnan's requirements.

Meanwhile, business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Tuesday that the industry group was finalising measures to bail out Musashino, centring on a plan to merge it with another Tokyo-based shinkin bank, Oji Shinkin Bank.
The plan calls for the Zenshinren Bank and 50 shinkin banks in Tokyo to grant funds to write off all of Musashino's unrecoverable loans, the newspaper said.

By merging Musashino with a healthy shinkin bank with the all-out support of the shinkin banking sector, the sector is keen to prevent the failure from causing further unrest, the newspaper quoted industry sources as saying.
